configuration.model: SUNCAT_MODEL changes the default brain model. SUNCAT_CHARACTER_MODEL, SUNCAT_GM_MODEL, SUNCAT_UTILITY_MODEL and SUNCAT_MODERATION_MODEL override their conversation roles.

configuration.relicCustody: One of each Hallow per saved personal story world, with a browser custody anchor and a copy inside the character save. Different offline worlds are independent; this is not global multiplayer trade authority.

limitations: Independent simulation covers ordinary authored inhabitants and herb nodes; residents do not require a human visit. Three authored road quests and guild contracts use Suncat’s own progress. Other scripted quest interfaces, dynamic summons, mining, fishing and autonomous smithing remain outside this pass.
Offscreen combat is a bounded rules simulation, not a rendered browser: supported hits resolve by range, obstruction, dice and wards rather than full projectile flight.
Local tests use controlled model replies; actual Gemini choices and older-phone performance require live gameplay testing.
World consequences retain up to 96 maps across saved worlds, with bounded receipts and conversation history.

Supported personal quest creatures retain their own receipts; story cinematics and other quest-specific interfaces are not falsely marked complete when no executable adapter exists. There is no blanket prohibition on meeting new NPCs or accepting quests.

Suncat uses the standard Talk/Use/Take/Break interaction control. His normal JRPG greeting is Yes? with Draw weapon, Talk and Leave; the separate Talk to Suncat button is removed.

Talk opens the live conversation and Back restores the choices. Draw weapon enables normal combat movement and allied targeting without sending an attack itself; an actual ceasefire clears that state.

Cherry retains her defender behavior after performing, with STR raised to 32d4. Her landed basic attack can finish an ordinary hostile fox when it breaks every ward. The performer-only nonlethal clash flag no longer prevents that result. Pets, bosses and quest foxes remain excluded.
Idle ordinary enemies cannot cross into Tintagel’s coastal town, river settlement or southeastern village. Active pursuits may cross those settlement boundaries.

Ordinary enemies avoid the area around Cherry’s tavern even during pursuit, do not select sheltered humans as targets, and retreat if already inside. Authored encounters, companions and other maps retain their existing movement rules.

Preserved v79 projectile cancellation, finite lifetimes, bounded attack list, Suncat server sanctuary, Cherry’s smooth 2x dance, previous quests and shop changes. Shared server and Dragonflight 11.67 networking are byte-identical to v79.
Tavern sanctuary cancels attacks using the real active flag, removes stalled visuals from the projectile list and reports Suncat cancellation once.

Ordinary projectiles expire after 30 seconds. Arrivals also sweep expired shots while simulation is paused; no more than 512 attacks are retained. Lingering gravity zones retain their authored duration.
All tavern occupants, including Cherry after her performance, avoid combat targeting. Hostile wildlife leaves alive along a bounded, body-sized terrain route; normal combat resumes outside.

Server-side Suncat respects the same sanctuary before spending combat resources, clears pending attacks on entry and rejects protected hostility without deciding mercy or changing character relationships.

Cherry performs the same smooth choreography at 2x speed: 36-second loop, with pose frames accelerated to match.
Class recommendations are trackable journal quests with current objective markers. Only spawned class-trial enemies gain boss markers.
One persistent network Suncat body uses one elected active client observer; handoffs fence stale commands and preserve world provenance. Other nearby clients render that body.
Perception uses Suncat-relative distance and sight, independent of the human camera. Nearby services and resources are supplied before autonomous decisions.

Peaceful proximity and collision open live Suncat conversation once per visited map per session; later contact passes through and manual conversation remains available. Deliberate attacks enable combat and allied targeting; accepted ceasefire clears it.
Attacks request a model decision instead of forcing retaliation. Suncat may choose speech, sustained defense, escape or ceasefire from real actions.

Character, GM, utility and moderation receive separate prompts, histories and capability checks. Mysticism and unawareness are no longer mandatory. Creator background is attributed separately from lived memory.
Moderation reports retain bounded recent server chat evidence and a pending-admin decision. Character favor cannot issue sanctions.
The existing opt-in generated GM scenario is restricted to one active region, actual objectives, existing once-only contract rewards, and cleanup after ten empty minutes.

Battle music starts from actual player damage, including ward loss and attributed damage over time; nearby fights and aggro alone are silent. The tavern clears a stuck card battle and restores actor visibility.
